clue.text: Eric it could be in the tall grass

parts.note: the name is what you get when the answer is read as an instruction: the second word, made wild, can become this name

explanation.surface: Someone named Eric might be lurking in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'it could be' tells you the answer, read as wordplay (the second word, run wild), produces the clue's name Eric, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: This aquatic plant of North American lakes is a tall reedy grass whose seeds are eaten as a grain.

clue.text: Over the years an Ascot lady may have quite a few different roles

definitions.text: Over the years an Ascot lady may
have quite a few different roles

explanation.surface: A society lady at the races builds up a collection of headgear while juggling many jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English race meeting famous for extravagant ladies' hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a racegoer puts on many hats over the years; idiomatically someone holding many jobs at once.

clue.text: Go left when coming to end of the avenue

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Turn left when you reach the end of the avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes only the last letter of 'the', E, not the end of the avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart or go away from a place is to quit it.

clue.text: Evidence of coastal erosion fishermen originally found in sea area

indicators.note: found in places the first letter inside the sea area's name

parts.note: Rockall is one of the sea areas of the BBC Shipping Forecast

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of fishermen

explanation.surface: Fishermen first spotted signs of a crumbling coast in a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCKALL is a sea area named in the BBC radio Shipping Forecast, broadcast for British waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapsing cliffs drop debris onto the shore, a sign that the sea is eating away the coast.

clue.text: Leader of church — that is, leader of fold

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of fold

explanation.surface: The head of the church, that is, the shepherd of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second an instruction to take the F.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a group or organisation is its principal or boss.

clue.text: French town's sausages not second-rate

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the place to its wordplay

indicators.note: not tells us one piece is dropped from the sausage word

parts.note: bangers is British slang for sausages
B, as in a B-grade or B-movie, means second-rate

explanation.surface: A French town is known for its sausages, which are not inferior.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGERS is everyday British slang for sausages; removing B leaves the Loire city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Loire is the historic capital of Anjou in western France.

clue.text: Not all may be sane brought up in a place of conflict

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the run is read from bottom to top
not all of the words are used, signalling a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some people raised in a war zone may not be entirely sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes letters from MAY BE SANE and 'brought up' turns them, reading YBESAN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This Northamptonshire village was the site of the decisive 1645 battle of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Banish old lover attired in awful fashion

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in awful fashion suggests the letters are badly arranged, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Send away the former partner who dresses terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banish' is a fair definition: extradition sends someone out of the country; 'in awful fashion' signals the rearrangement of 'attired'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand someone over to another country for trial is to expel them from where they are.

clue.text: Do repeated screams, wolf on the loose being an imminent threat

indicators.note: on the loose suggests the letters running free, so they are rearranged
repeated means the word do is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keep screaming because a wolf has escaped and danger looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles DO, and 'on the loose' rearranges DODO + SCREAMS + WOLF, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek tale a blade hung by one hair above the courtier's head, so it means a peril hanging over someone.

clue.text: Fish upsetting one's gut around the end of supper

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the last letter of supper
upsetting suggests disturbing the order of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters ONES

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of supper

explanation.surface: Eating fish has upset someone's stomach by the end of supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges ONESGUT and 'around' wraps it round R, the last letter of supper.
explanation.definitionFit: This large fish is prized for its roe, which is caviar.

clue.text: An impish saint, one held to be a subversive character

parts.note: taken as written
arch can mean mischievous or impish, as in an arch smile
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mischievous holy figure turns out to be a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impish' is the adjective arch, as in an arch look, not a bishop's rank; 'held' signals that the numeral sits inside the saint's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants to overthrow all government and authority is the archetypal subversive.

clue.text: Fight in beastly home coming to nothing

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow, an animal's home
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out in some animal's den and comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A sett is the burrow of a badger, the beast of 'beastly home'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief heated quarrel or scrap is commonly called this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Bundle female placed behind nut tree

indicators.note: placed behind tells us the female abbreviation goes after the tree

parts.note: the shea is an African tree whose nuts yield shea butter

explanation.surface: A woman puts a bundle down behind a nut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female' wants to be SHE, but it is only F; the SHEA tree supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalks of corn bound together after reaping make one of these harvest bundles.

clue.text: Troublemaker given support when fantastic friend comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the scrambled friend surrounds the support garment
fantastic suggests wild and fanciful, so the letters of friend are rearranged

parts.note: a bra is an item of supportive underwear

explanation.surface: A wild friend arrives to help out a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is the crossword's favourite underwear; 'fantastic' signals the rearrangement of 'friend', and 'comes round' says that rearrangement encloses the support.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up unrest or strife is figuratively a burning torch thrown into a crowd.

clue.text: Being left empty, sick inside, dithered

indicators.note: inside places the word for sick within the word for left empty

parts.note: vacated means left empty, as a room someone moves out of
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone left feeling empty and sick hesitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is only a link; 'inside' signals that the word for sick sits within the word for left empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver back and forth without deciding is to hesitate or dither.

clue.text: Domestic delight concealing endless misery — a nightmare's beginning

indicators.note: concealing means the trimmed misery word hides inside the word for delight

parts.note: to charm is to delight

indicators.note: endless means the misery word loses its final letter

parts.note: woe means misery

indicators.note: beginning means take the first letter of nightmare's

explanation.surface: A delightful home help hides her endless misery before a nightmare begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' is a noun here, a household servant; 'endless' trims the misery word and 'concealing' hides it within the delight word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning woman employed in a house is a domestic worker, a domestic for short.

clue.text: Sailor beaming, not one seen as scratchy type?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: not means the numeral for one is dropped from the beaming word

parts.note: radiant means beaming
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grinning sailor, not a single one, looks like an itchy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor; RADIANT less I gives RADANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears away a surface by scraping, like sandpaper, is an abrasive, hence the playful scratchy type.

clue.text: Irish backing to accompany very loud bit of music

indicators.note: backing signals that the abbreviation for Irish is read backwards

parts.note: FF stands for fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: An Irish backing band accompanies a loud passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IR into RI; FF is the musical marking fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: A short repeated phrase played on guitar or other instrument is a musical figure of this kind.

clue.text: See hippy type look no good with hard expression

parts.note: lo means look or see
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a look or expression on someone's face

explanation.surface: Behold a hippy whose look is bad and whose expression is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing at the hippy; the pieces are LO + NG + H + AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with long hair, especially a hippy or intellectual, was nicknamed this in the 1960s.

clue.text: Prepared to take year off for study

indicators.note: to take the year off means the abbreviation for year is removed

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to take a gap year for studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take ... off' removes Y from READY; the surface suggests a gap year.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at university, especially in Britain, is to read it: she read law.

clue.text: Entertainment provided by female member of family, idiot artist

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a female relative
a dope is a fool or idiot
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A show is put on by grandma, a fool and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully sung, serious operatic work is a form of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Big building left half-abandoned with shed taking priority

indicators.note: taking priority means the shed word comes first in the answer

parts.note: cast means shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: half-abandoned means half of left is dropped, keeping its first half

explanation.surface: A big building was left half-abandoned, a shed being built first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-abandoned' keeps only the first half of 'left', and 'taking priority' puts the shed word ahead of it; 'Big building' looks like a phrase about the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fortified residence of a lord or monarch is a massive building.

clue.text: Scot — mean person coming down to earth?

parts.note: low can mean mean or base
a lander is something, here jokingly someone, that touches down on a surface

explanation.surface: A Scot is called mean, someone who has to come back down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the stereotype of Scots as mean; the question mark covers the playful sense of one who lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the southern and eastern lowlands of Scotland, as opposed to the Highlands.

clue.text: Approach old character briefly at Oxford?

indicators.note: briefly means the old character word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
to be up is to be in residence at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Approaching an old eccentric briefly while at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old character' suggests an elderly eccentric, but it is a RUNE; students at Oxford or Cambridge are said to be up.
explanation.definitionFit: The period or route leading up to something, such as a bowler's approach to the crease, is called this.

clue.text: Lizard creating 'ell in the course of journey

indicators.note: in the course of puts the dropped-aitch expletive inside the journey

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip, a journey
hell with its H dropped, and heck is the mild form of hell, so 'eck

explanation.surface: Someone's travels are made hell by a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' is a link: as 'ell drops the H from hell, so 'eck drops it from heck, the polite substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: This small lizard of warm countries can climb walls with its sticky toe pads.

clue.text: Revolutionary bound by firm set of beliefs

indicators.note: bound by means the revolutionary is enclosed by the firm abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary tied to a firm creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective meaning fixed, but it is the noun, a company, giving CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith or guiding principles is a creed, Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Allow notice to be placed at front of American university

indicators.text: to be placed at front of
indicators.note: to be placed at front of tells us the notice comes before the university

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Permission is given for a notice to be put up at the front of a US college.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone in, or to concede, is to grant entry or permission.

clue.text: Super model made to look awful in alien porn

indicators.note: made to look awful suggests the words are mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supermodel is degraded by appearing in alien pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to look awful' rearranges ALIEN PORN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon with no equal is a perfect model of excellence.

clue.text: Someone of note, an inventor who got everything sewn up?

definitions.text: an inventor who got everything sewn up?

explanation.surface: A person of fame, an inventor who settled everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Merritt Singer developed and sold the sewing machine, hence 'sewn up', which also means settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist produces musical notes, and the American inventor gave his name to the famous sewing machine company.

clue.text: Birds in at least three quarrels?

parts.note: to spar is to argue, giving one quarrel
rows are quarrels, at least two of them, making three or more in all

explanation.surface: Birds are caught up in a number of arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: One spar plus two or more rows makes at least three quarrels; the question mark flags the arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: These small brown songbirds are among the commonest garden birds.
